problem_pattern: Question says 'the X in Y' or 'the X of Y'
guidance: Do NOT assume X is Y. Find Y first, then search for sub-entities of type X related to Y (e.g., RunSPARQL: SELECT ?x WHERE { ?x prop:located_in ex:Y . ?x prop:instance_of ex:town . }).

problem_pattern: Question asks for a single qualifier on an attribute or relation statement (When / Where / What role / What ceremony / Since when / In what gender)
guidance: ALWAYS prefer over GetEdgeQualifiers / GetQualifiersByPredicate / GetAttributeWithQualifiers when you can name the qualifier from the wh-word. GetQualifierValue(subject, predicate, target, qualifier_name) projects ONLY that qualifier — auto-detects relation vs attribute, auto-handles forward/backward direction, returns one clean value with no full-dict scan and no chance of selecting the wrong key. Wh-word -> qualifier name map: 'When' -> point_in_time, 'Since when / from when' -> start_time, 'Until when' -> end_time, 'Where' -> location, 'What role / In what role' -> object_has_role, 'What ceremony / At which event' -> ceremony, 'For what work / For which film' -> for_work, 'What language' -> language, 'What part / Which form / Masc/fem' -> applies_to_part, 'What case' -> criterion_used / grammatical_case.

problem_pattern: DISCOVERY ONLY: you do not yet know which qualifier names exist on a statement
guidance: Use this ONLY when the wh-word does not pin a single qualifier (e.g., 'For what' is ambiguous between for_work and ceremony) AND you genuinely need the full qualifier dict to choose. The moment you know the qualifier name, switch to GetQualifierValue. Calling GetEdgeQualifiers and visually scanning the dict is the most common qualifier-extraction failure mode — the LLM tends to pick the most prominent key, not the correct one.

problem_pattern: Need attribute value AND its temporal/spatial context
guidance: Use this when you need both the attribute value and its qualifiers (e.g., population with point_in_time). If qualifiers are missing, fall back to GetEdgeQualifiers which uses the reification pattern.

problem_pattern: Question asks for a value 'in [year]' or 'as of [date]'
guidance: Use this for date-filtered attribute lookups. It handles date comparison automatically. Increase tolerance_days if exact date match fails.

problem_pattern: Genuinely 3+ hop joins or unusual patterns not expressible via existing tools
guidance: LAST RESORT only. For Count, use CountEntities (handles or_conditions and transitive_concept). For SelectAmong/SelectBetween, use SelectExtreme. For Verify (existence), use VerifyFact. Reach for RunSPARQL only when the question genuinely needs a multi-relation join or an aggregation pattern none of the typed tools cover. Do NOT define namespace prefixes — the server injects them automatically.

ALWAYS prefer over FilterEntities + len() (which truncates at limit=50) and over hand-written RunSPARQL COUNT (error-prone with KQAPro namespaces). Returns the EXACT count. For OR conditions, pass or_conditions=[{...}]. For concept hierarchies (e.g. 'all mammals' covering subspecies), set transitive_concept=True.

problem_pattern: SelectAmong (superlative over a typed group) or SelectBetween (compare 2 entities)
guidance: ALWAYS prefer over CompareEntities + manual pick. Returns the actual winner via SPARQL ORDER BY. SelectAmong: pass concept + attribute_name + mode='max'|'min'. SelectBetween: pass entity_ids=[id_A, id_B] + attribute_name + mode. Dates: mode='min' = earliest = older. filter_attribute_* applies a pre-filter before ranking.

problem_pattern: Verify question that asks if a specific fact exists
guidance: ALWAYS prefer over GetAttributeDetails-then-empty-means-no for fact-existence questions. Single SPARQL ASK, deterministic boolean. predicate_type='auto' tries attribute first, then relation. For numeric/date COMPARISONS, still use VerifyNumericCondition; VerifyFact handles equality/existence only.

problem_pattern: Question contains a unique ID, code, URL, or ISNI
guidance: Use this for exact reverse lookup instead of FindNode. Pass the value and attribute name (e.g., FindByAttribute('0000 0004 0631 7316', 'ISNI')).

problem_pattern: Need to find entities connected via a specific relation
guidance: Returns all target entities for a relation. If 0 results, try the inverse direction or check available_predicates from FindNode for the correct relation name.

problem_pattern: Need to compare an attribute across 2+ entities
guidance: Pass a list of entity IDs and the comparison attribute. Returns sorted results. More efficient than calling GetAttributeDetails on each entity separately.

problem_pattern: Need to compare two numbers or dates
guidance: NEVER perform mental math. Always pass numeric comparisons to this tool. It handles type coercion and returns a reliable True/False verdict.
